prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D geometry as the camera wearer climbs up a wooden ladder or scaffolding pole (0.3–1.2 m away on the left) alongside a close vertical brick and concrete structure on the right (0.4–1.0 m away), above a ground surface strewn with sacks roughly 1.5–2.5 m below. Across frames 1 to 4, the camera wearer ascends toward an upper brick ledge where a round mortar pan rests about 0.8–1.5 m ahead on the left and a second person's bare leg and lowered hand stand in the shadowed area behind it at roughly 1.2–1.8 m away. In frame 5, the viewpoint turns and rises to the upper level where the second person bends forward directly in front of the camera wearer within arm's reach (0.2–0.8 m), extending their left arm toward the foreground over a pile of wet mortar (~0.5–1.0 m below) while holding a trowel in their right hand (~0.7 m away). The depth map reveals the continuous 3D surface of the recessed brick ledge, the mortar pan, and the second person's leg in the dark shadow of frame 4—details that are obscured by harsh sunlight and deep shadow in the RGB image. However, the map is somewhat unreliable where it smooths over the individual bricks and sacks on the ground, and in frame 5 where the bright foreground arm and underlying mortar pile partially blend in depth.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates only partial human regions labeled as 'person' against a black background, missing all surrounding structural elements like the ladder pole, brick walls, mortar pan, and pile of mortar. In frames 2 and 3, a pink mask at the bottom center-right captures the camera wearer's own right forearm, gloved hand, and lower torso/skirt at 0.2–0.5 m from the lens, though it completely misses the camera wearer's lower body in frame 1. In frame 4, the map segments the second person's bare leg and descending hand in the upper center at roughly 1.2–1.8 m ahead (about 0.5 m behind the unsegmented mortar pan), with their upper body cropped out of the top of the frame. By frame 5, as the camera wearer reaches the upper platform, a large mask covers the second person's torso, legs, and outstretched arms bending toward the camera wearer from 0.2–1.0 m away, with their head occluded above the top frame boundary and their hands within arm's reach of both the mortar pile and the camera wearer. While the segmentation map makes it easier to spot the second person's leg and hand inside the dark shadow of frame 4 than in the high-contrast RGB frame, it is unreliable for overall scene layout because it omits all tools and construction structures, drops the wearer's body in frames 1 and 4, and has jagged mask boundaries around the person's lower legs in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all five frames, failing to detect any body or hand skeletons despite the presence of both the camera wearer and a second person in the RGB strip. In the RGB context, the camera wearer's own right arm and hand appear at the bottom right of frames 2 and 3 (0.3–0.5 m away, within arm's reach of the ladder pole and brick wall), and the second person appears in frames 4 and 5 at distances shrinking from roughly 1.5 m to 0.2–0.8 m as the camera wearer climbs up and turns right. Because the second person's head and shoulders are consistently occluded by the top edge of the frame—showing only a leg and hand in the dark shadow of frame 4, and a downward-bending torso with an outstretched left arm (~0.2 m from the camera) and right hand gripping a trowel (~0.7 m away) in frame 5—the pose estimator fails to initialize any keypoints. In frame 5, the RGB shows the second person facing downward and slightly left toward the mortar pile rather than looking directly at the camera wearer, with both hands within reach of the mortar and the left hand within reach of the camera wearer. Consequently, the pose map provides no spatial information beyond the RGB and is entirely unreliable under these severe ego-view truncations, top-edge head occlusions, and extreme close-up foreshortening.
